items.title: Use NUL-delimited Git paths in the Step 4 owner inventory guard
items.body:
The first actual Step 4 dependency-chain dispatch for #1005 stopped before invoking any native build command because the run-owned inventory guard parsed Git filenames incorrectly.

`native_chain.py` uses `git ls-tree -r --name-only BASE data/ingredients`, splits on newlines, and retains strings ending in `.yaml`. Git quotes and escapes non-ASCII filenames by default, so five existing owners end in a closing quote and are dropped. The actual ignored-inclusive filesystem inventory contains the unchanged 2,955 owners; the parsed baseline contains only 2,950. This falsely reports changed membership.

Affected existing names include `L-α-phosphatidylinositol_From_Glycine_Max_Soybean.yaml`, `Α-lipoic_Acid.yaml`, `Α1-Acid_Glycoprotein_From_Bovine_Plasma.yaml`, `Poly-ß-hydroxybutyric_Acid.yaml`, and `Α-D-Glucose_Monohydrate.yaml`.

Evidence: driver SHA256 `75c29e50c75fd6ee4acfc5c2b8402da634ee286f7ae8054958e656b368a21a13`; base `838d0c2627552b0094545ebb580b5bb9b1a84d57`; failed native dispatch log `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/logs/step4-dispatch-chain-build.log` SHA256 `3d4f1b110a70aaa4d37ee91a6267df49cfcbae1f3976cb23a91c64f32d3c0241`. The separate post-application comparison already verified one changed owner and 2,954 unchanged owners. No native chain output was produced by this failed dispatch.

Severity: low, false refusal in execution guard. Use Git's NUL-delimited filename output and parse exact filename bytes/text without quote interpretation. Add a regression using real Git entries with non-ASCII filenames, and retain rejection of actual added/removed owner paths. Independently re-review before rerunning the chain. This is a run-owned driver defect, not a request to rename ingredient files or weaken ignored-file inventory coverage.

items.title: 87 published labels resolve to more than one identifier, including 18 preferred_term-vs-synonym collisions
items.body:
Found reviewing #231, which introduces the ambiguity by publishing synonyms.

Before #231, `docs/data/*.csv` carried only `preferred_term`, and **preferred_terms are unique** (verified: zero duplicates). So the CSV supported an unambiguous `{label: identifier}` join. Publishing synonyms makes that join order-dependent for **87 labels**.

The sharp cases are where **one record's `preferred_term` is another record's synonym** — a consumer's answer depends purely on row order:

| label | holders |
|---|---|
| `Vitamin B12` | CHEBI:176843 (preferred) / CHEBI:17439 (synonym) / UNMAPPED_0005 (synonym) |
| `Mannitol` | CHEBI:29864 (preferred) / CHEBI:16899 (synonym) |
| `Tryptophan` | CHEBI:27897 (preferred) / CHEBI:16828 (synonym) |
| `Citrate` | CHEBI:16947 (preferred) / CHEBI:30769 (synonym) |
| `Sulfur` | CHEBI:26833 (preferred) / CHEBI:17909 (synonym) |
| `Putrescine` | CHEBI:17148 (preferred) / cas:333-93-7 (synonym) |

…and ~12 more of that shape.

Some of these are the #218 family in another guise — `Citrate`/`Citric acid`, `Sulfur`, `Mannitol` are the same substance under two CHEBI ids, i.e. the inverse defect of #225. Others are legitimately shared synonyms where two distinct terms both accept a loose common name.

#231 does **not** treat this as a failure — a synonym legitimately can be shared, and failing the build on it would block the fix. The gate prints it as a note.

## What to decide

1. Which of the 87 are the #225/#218 inverse defect (one substance, two ids) and should be merged, versus genuinely-shared loose names.
2. For the genuine ones, whether the published surface should carry a precedence signal so a consumer can resolve deterministically — e.g. a `match_type` column distinguishing preferred_term from synonym, so `Vitamin B12` → CHEBI:176843 is the documented answer.

Until (2), consumers joining on the `synonyms` column should prefer a row whose `preferred_term` equals the query.

Related: #231, #229, #218, #225.

items.title: Retire 4 residual duplicates via the synonym pass (#208)
items.body:
Addresses #208. **Stacked on #271 → #269** (base `fix/196-source-occurrences`); retarget down the stack as each merges.

## What #208 asked for

Seven residual labels researched as "net-new" in PR #202 turned out to already be mapped in MIM under a canonical label. Force-promoting them would mint an identifier another record already holds — the defect `just qc-duplicate-ids` gates — so they were parked for a curator synonym pass.

**Four needed the pass and got it**, each carrying the residual label over as a `RAW_TEXT` synonym plus its `kgmicrobe.trait` source_id into the target's `curation_history`:

| residual | → target | why |
|---|---|---|
| Alpha-hydroxybutyrate | CHEBI:64552 *2-hydroxybutyrate* | alpha/2- positional naming |
| Beta-hydroxybutyrate | CHEBI:37054 *3-hydroxybutyrate* | beta/3- positional naming |
| Achromycin | CHEBI:27902 *Tetracycline* | trade name |
| Neomycin E | CHEBI:7934 *Paromomycin* | synonym |

**Two were already done** — `Glycogen` and `Arabitol` already carry `(+)-D-glycogen` and `(+)-L-lyxitol`. No action needed; verified rather than assumed.

Unmapped residual **513 → 509**.

## The seventh (RNA) is deliberately not merged

That is precisely what #208 asks: *"generic RNA must not merge onto the specific Torula-yeast product record."* No merge was performed.

Finishing the **split**, though, is blocked. `Ribonucleic acid from torula yeast type VI` holds `CHEBI:33697 "ribonucleic acid"` at EXACT_MATCH — over-claiming, and occupying the CURIE that the label which genuinely *is* generic RNA should hold. The fix requires moving the Torula record onto a `kgmicrobe.compound:` mint with a `narrowMatch`, and `reground_mapped_record.py` refuses any destination it cannot resolve in an ontology adapter:

```
kgmicrobe.compound:ribonucleic_acid_from_torula_yeast_type_vi has no rdfs:label in chebi.db
```

Filed as **#273** rather than worked around — hand-editing a re-ground is exactly what #267 was filed about, and how PR #266 minted two duplicate identifiers.

## Verification

Canary first: one merge applied and verified **against the collections the tool actually writes**, not the per-record files (which are regenerated later, and where my first check looked in the wrong place and read as a false negative). Confirmed the synonym attached, `MERGED_FROM_UNMAPPED_DUPLICATE` history written, and the source removed from the unmapped collection — then the remaining three.

- `just validate-strict` → **0 ERROR rows**; `reconcile_sssom` → in sync (GAP/ORPHAN/STALE all 0)
- `just qc-duplicate-ids` → matches baseline; `just validate-products` → exit 0
- **714 tests pass**; the single failure (`test_check_chebi_currency`) is pre-existing and fails identically on `main`.

items.title: Retire a parent's names from the records of its salts and hydrates (#232)
items.body:
Addresses #232's `conflict:different_substances` core: **47 → 11**, colliding labels **111 → 75**.

## The shape

40 of the 47 conflicts are one thing: a salt, hydrate or merge-tombstone record carries the name of the parent it is a form *of* — the free acid's IUPAC name on a monopotassium salt, the anhydrous ChEBI label on a heptahydrate, a sibling hydrate's formula string on a tombstone. MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 makes those distinct substances, so a consumer resolving the parent's name reached the wrong one.

| record | retired | why |
|---|---|---|
| `L-Glutamic_Acid_Monopotassium_Salt_Monohydrate` | `(2S)-2-aminopentanedioic acid`, `GLUTAMIC ACID` | ChEBI names of `CHEBI:16015` / `CHEBI:18237`, the acid |
| `Feso4_X_7h2o` (tombstone) | `FeSO4 x 6 H2O` ×4, `FeSO4 x 5 H2O`, `iron(2+) sulfate`… | hexa/penta-hydrate strings and the anhydrous label on a heptahydrate |
| `Cecl3_X_7_H2o` | `cerium(III) chloride`, `cerium(3+) chloride`, `trichloridocerium` | ChEBI names of anhydrous `CHEBI:35458` |
| `Sn-Glycerol_3-phosphate_Lithium_Salt` | `(2R)-2,3-dihydroxypropyl dihydrogen phosphate` | the free phosphate's name, `CHEBI:15978` |

**57 synonyms on 23 records**, all `REJECTED_LABEL` (never deleted — claw filters rebuilds through rejected labels).

## How they were verified

The 40 proposals came from one reader each; the adversarial skeptic stage never ran (session limit, then credits). So they were verified **mechanically**, with a criterion that needs no judgement and is re-derived from ChEBI on every run: *the synonym is a name ChEBI gives another mapped record's term and not this record's own, or a formula whose water count differs from this record's.* 57 pass. Names ChEBI does not carry (a CultureBotHT spelling of a-ketoglutaric acid, `Na2-citrate`) are **left for a curator**, not guessed.

## Blast radius, measured

A rebuild of the unified mapping on pristine `main` vs this branch: **14 rows change, all synonyms, 0 mappings lost, 1 identity moves** — `Aspartic acid` now resolves to the free acid `CHEBI:17053` instead of the potassium salt `cas:1115-63-5`, which is the point.

## `qc-unified-freshness` is red, and should be

62 record files have changed since the committed snapshot's stamp against a budget of 25; **39 are upstream** (#699, #708). The remedy is a rebuild, and I did not install one: against current claw it drops **15 mappings this branch never touches** (Vitamin B12 → an unmapped "Vitamin B12 Solution" record, Betaine, Corn meal agar). That is a builder question, recorded on #700, and needs its own reviewed row-set diff.

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `validate-all` / `qc-sssom` (A–L) / `qc-roundtrip` / `qc-flat-coverage` / `check-unified-rejections` | pass |
| `check-unified-freshness` | **red — drift budget, see above** |
| `lint` / `format-check` / `typecheck` / `check-instruction-refs` | clean |
| `sync-curated` re-cased | 0 files |

items.title: Add organic-acid carbon-source inference (coverage 40.2% → 43.2%)
items.body:
## Summary
Pushes into the role-coverage long tail with a curated organic-acid carbon-source rule.

### Coverage 40.2% → 43.2% (+56 roles)
Adds a canonical organic-acid rule to `infer_roles_from_name_lists.py`: TCA/glycolysis/short-chain acids (acetate, lactate, pyruvate, succinate, fumarate, malate, citrate, propionate, butyrate, formate, gluconate, 2-oxoglutarate, glutarate, glycolate, malonate, caproate, octanoate, hydroxybutyrate, quinate, shikimate, …) as `-ate`/`-ic acid` → **CARBON_SOURCE**.

**Why a curated list, not CHEBI ancestry:** ancestry files the common *salt* forms (sodium acetate, pyruvate) under "salt", not carboxylic acid — so it misses them. **Why a blocklist:** name-matching alone over-tags. A metal/ester/aromatic/ammonium blocklist (verified against the full candidate set) excludes:
- toxic-metal acetates — `Cadmium`/`Thallium`/`Uranyl acetate`
- metal-citrate complexes (iron/Mg sources) — `Ferric citrate`, `Mg-citrate`
- esters / ionic liquids — `ethyl acetate`, imidazolium acetate
- aromatic / indole acids — `Phenyl acetic acid`, `Indole-3-butyric acid`
- ammonium salts (nitrogen) — `(NH4)2 citrate`

All 56 matches are individually-vetted clean carbon sources; oxalate was deliberately left out (borderline chelator). **812 roles / 808 records, 0 validation errors.**

The remaining ~1060 unroled records are the genuine residue — complete named media (correctly unroled), and uncharacterized/ambiguous MESH/NCIT/CAS entries that need true per-record curation rather than pattern rules.

## Tests
+8 cases pinning organic-acid positives and the blocklist exclusions; `Citrate` reclassified excluded→CARBON_SOURCE.

## Validation
- `validate_strict.py`: **0 errors / 2274 files**
- `validate_roles.py`: **812 roles, 0 errors, 100% cited**
- Full suite: **295 passed**

## Summary
Follow-ups from the roles/obsolete-CHEBI work (PR #36), in three commits.

Three enantiomers that an earlier auto-upgrade collapsed onto their achiral CHEBI parent are re-pointed to the correct stereospecific terms (verified against the local CHEBI sqlite):
- `(R)-3-hydroxybutyrate`: CHEBI:37054 → **CHEBI:10983**

- `L-Carnitine`: CHEBI:17126 → **CHEBI:16347** ((R)-carnitine); DL-carnitine keeps CHEBI:17126

### Broaden role coverage 22.8% → 33.2%
New `infer_roles_from_name_lists.py`: high-precision curated name-pattern inference for the categories CHEBI-ancestry deliberately skips:
- antibiotics → SELECTIVE_AGENT (148)
- nutrient metal salts → MINERAL (33, matched by formula prefix — avoids the azide/dithionite false positives)
- reductants → REDUCING_AGENT (7)

items.body:
## Summary
Brings the external SSSOM mapping deliverable back in sync with the curated data, and verifies the chemical-properties gap.

### SSSOM sync (task #1)
`mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` had drifted: it has **no generator** (only a validator + `qc-sssom` invariant gate, which doesn't check currency), so the identifier remaps from PRs #36/#37/#40 never propagated. New **`scripts/sync_sssom_remaps.py`** surgically updates only the affected subjects, leaving the rest of the bespoke file (multi-row Rule-B1 registry rows, pipeline-provenance columns, custom subject_id encoding) byte-for-byte intact:
- **removed**: `CHEBI:1` (record deleted), `Bacto Soytone` (now REJECTED/merged)
- `(R)`/`(S)-3-hydroxybutyrate`: `CHEBI:37054` → `CHEBI:10983` / `CHEBI:11047`
- `L-Carnitine`: `CHEBI:17126` → `CHEBI:16347`
- `Tryptone` → `MICRO:0000182` (now exactMatch); `Trypticase` → `MICRO:0000175`

Diff is 7 changed rows + the header version/date. **0 stale identifiers remain**; passes `validate_sssom_invariants` Rules A/B1/B2/B3.

> A full from-scratch SSSOM *generator* remains a known gap (the file encodes lost pipeline state); the surgical syncer keeps it current with minimal risk and is re-runnable for future remaps.

### Chemical-properties enrichment (task #3) — verified, no change
Ran the enricher on the 24 CHEBI records lacking a `chemical_properties` block: **all 24 are genuinely formula-less** in both OLS/PubChem and the local CHEBI sqlite — abstract classes (Aromatic compound, Hydrocarbon, Surfactant), polymers (Xylan, Glycogen, LPS, poly-L-lysine), and macromolecules (Catalase, Elastin, DNA, LL-37). The gap is real, not an API failure, so there's nothing to enrich.

### UMAP regeneration (task #2)
The UMAP regen (`generate_ingredient_umap.py`) is re-reading the 3.2 GB embeddings file (cache miss) and is taking >25 min in this environment. It's a cosmetic visualization refresh; rather than block this correctness fix, it's running separately and will be added here or as a small follow-up once it completes.
